reconstruction: The counterexample has no atoms, so endpoint conventions cannot explain away the failure. Its total mass is one. The boundedness of this particular integral operator follows directly from Cauchy--Schwarz.
fate: A repaired one-sided statement is classical: a positive continuous probability density on \([a,b]\), with lower integration limit \(a\), is transformed by its cumulative distribution into ordinary Volterra integration. The latter lattice is given by \citet[Example~3]{donoghue1957lattice}. This does not validate the two-sided source formula, and no general unresolved measure classification is inferred from that false conjecture.
present_status: As of November 2026: false under the literal two-sided formulation; the indicated regular one-sided repair is established.

title: Bishop operators as possible invariant-subspace counterexamples
notes: The weighted composition operator is specialized to \(Tf(x)=x f(x+\alpha\bmod1)\), irrational \(\alpha\). It is proposed as having no invariant subspace, equivalently every vector cyclic.
statement: For irrational \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(T_\alpha f(x)=x f(\{x+\alpha\})\) on complex \(L^2(0,1)\). Does every such operator have a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace? The source\textquotesingle s contrary suggestion is false for many parameters, but the universal affirmative question is a distinct remaining problem. The equivalence with cyclicity requires every nonzero vector, not the zero vector.
fate: Davie\textquotesingle s 1974 theorem covers non-Liouville parameters; \citet[Theorem~3.7]{chamizo2020bishop} extends this to convergent denominators satisfying \(\log q_{j+1}=O(q_j/(\log q_j)^3)\), and hence includes some Liouville numbers. The same paper proves biquasitriangularity and norm approximation by nilpotent operators, neither of which alone produces an invariant subspace. \citet[Introduction]{behani2023bishop} explicitly retains the all-irrational question.
present_status: As of November 2026: the checked established results cover the stated arithmetic class, not every irrational parameter. No established all-parameter resolution was verified; the original no-subspace suggestion is already disproved for non-Liouville parameters.
worth: Yes. Exact finite-rotation products and quantitative rational approximation give concrete test cases. An invariant-subspace proof for the exceptional arithmetic regime still requires an argument beyond the finite-orbit continuity developed here.

title: Cyclic vectors for irrational Bishop operators
notes: After conjecturing that every vector is cyclic, the speaker says that not even one cyclic vector is known.
statement: For each irrational \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), does there exist \(f\in L^2(0,1)\) with \(\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{T_\alpha^n f:n\ge0\}=L^2(0,1)\)? A stronger concrete question asks when the constant function \(1\) is cyclic. Existence of one cyclic vector is far weaker than every nonzero vector being cyclic.
fate: \citet[Theorems~4.4--4.5, 4.9 and 4.16]{behani2023bishop} establishes rational cyclicity, a co-meager set of cyclic irrational parameters, and sufficient continued-fraction conditions. The preprint circulated in July 2022 and the paper appeared in 2023. Its Question~5.4 asks for an explicit approximation threshold. The chapter gives a bounded rational-fibre certificate and continuity estimate, not an all-irrational proof. A 2026 preprint lead was inaccessible and is not used as an established result.
present_status: As of November 2026: cyclicity is established for a co-meager parameter set and explicit sufficient classes in the checked work; universal irrational cyclicity was not verified. The historical absence of any known vector is obsolete.
worth: Yes. Rational cyclicity, exact finite products and strong continuity reduce selected questions to finite polynomial approximations with controlled error. The chapter develops such certificates and states their remaining arithmetic and conditioning obstacles explicitly.

title: The unspecified Ornstein cyclicity example
notes: An operator on \(L^2(0,1)\) is attributed to Ornstein, with every vector in \(L^{2+\varepsilon}\) cyclic. A nonsingular transformation without invariant measure is mentioned, but no operator is written.
statement: At minimum the cyclicity assertion must concern nonzero vectors and specify whether \(\varepsilon>0\) is fixed or varies. The operator, weight, transformation, and intended class of invariant measures are absent. A nonsingular transformation alone does not specify a bounded weighted-composition operator with the asserted cyclicity.
fate: Targeted searches on Ornstein, cyclic vectors, \(L^{2+\varepsilon}\), nonsingular transformations and invariant measures did not produce an opened primary theorem with these exact hypotheses. This anecdote is not identified with unrelated Ornstein results in ergodic theory, and no claimed counterexample to the Hilbert invariant-subspace problem is extracted from it.
present_status: As of November 2026: insufficiently specified and not securely identified; retained with explicit search limits.

title: Why invariant subspaces, and what could replace them?
notes: Gelfand asks why invariant subspaces are needed and what could replace them.
statement: This is a methodological question about structural invariants and operator models, not a quantified mathematical conjecture. Spectral measures, characteristic functions, similarity invariants and invariant-subspace lattices answer different versions of it.
fate: The next intervention gives one concrete contemporary response through analytic characteristic functions. No solved/open status is meaningful for the unrestricted methodological question itself.
present_status: As of November 2026: historical methodological discussion, not an independently unresolved theorem.

title: Analytic characteristic functions and the contraction model
notes: An English-speaking visitor with an uncertain F-name describes an analytic contraction from \(E\) to \(E_*\), Hardy boundary functions and analogues of Jordan blocks. The final finite-dimensional affine-map sentence does not specify the equivalence relation.
statement: For a completely nonunitary contraction \(T\), its characteristic function \(\Theta_T(z):\mathcal D_T\to\mathcal D_{T^*}\) is analytic and contractive for \(|z|<1\). It determines \(T\) up to unitary equivalence, modulo constant unitary identifications of the defect spaces. The standard model uses \([H^2(\mathcal D_{T^*})\oplus\overline{\Delta L^2(\mathcal D_T)}]\ominus\{\Theta_T f\oplus\Delta f:f\in H^2(\mathcal D_T)\}\), with \(\Delta=(I-\Theta_T^*\Theta_T)^{1/2}\).
reconstruction: The missing upper Fourier-integral limit is \(2\pi\); the positive exponent \(e^{int}\), \(n\ge1\), correctly kills negative Fourier coefficients. Complete nonunitarity and the defect-space constraints are essential. The separate finite-dimensional affine-map/Jordan analogy remains underdetermined.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1, p.~50; Theorem~3, p.~58]{sznagyfoias1964viii} gives the model and complete unitary invariant; it was received April 1963, revised December 1963 and published in 1964. \citet[Theorem~1 and formulas (3.16)--(3.17), pp.~294--295]{sznagyfoias1964ix} gives the factorization/invariant-subspace correspondence. This is an exact mathematical match, but not independent proof of the visitor\textquotesingle s identity.
present_status: As of November 2026: established with the hypotheses in the modern statement.
